records.title: Installing dex
records.text: Assuming you’ve already installed the D compiler (DMD or LDC) and DUB, creating a new dex project takes less than a minute. Prerequisites dex requires DMD 2.100+ or LDC 1.30+ along with the DUB package manager. If you haven't installed them yet, you can get them using the official installer script: Terminal $ curl -fsS https://dlang.org/install.sh | bash -s dmd Step 1: Create a Project Directory Create a directory to hold your application and make it your working directory: Terminal $ mkdir myapp $ cd myapp Step 2: Initialize DUB Project Use dub init to create a minimal application descriptor: Terminal $ dub init -t minimal -n Step 3: Install dex Add dex as a dependency to your dub.json file: Terminal $ dub add dex Alternatively, you can edit your dub.json directly to include dex: dub.json { "name": "myapp", "description": "My web application", "dependencies": { "dex": "~>0.5.0" } } Manual Installation (Without DUB) Because dex has zero external runtime dependencies (relying purely on standard Phobos and druntime), you do not need DUB to build or run applications. You can compile directly with DMD or LDC. Option A: Direct Compilation with -i (Compiler-Assisted Imports) Clone dex or include it as a git submodule: Terminal $ git clone https://github.com/ernlel/dex.git Use D's automatic import compiler flag (-i) to compile your application and link dex modules in one step: Terminal # With DMD $ dmd -i -Idex/source app.d -of=myapp # With LDC $ ldc2 -i -Idex/source app.d -of=myapp Option B: Build Static Library (libdex.a) via Makefile You can build a standalone static library archive using the included Makefile: Terminal $ cd dex $ make $ make test $ sudo make install # Installs to /usr/local/lib and /usr/local/include/d/dex Then compile your project linking against libdex.a: Terminal $ dmd -I/usr/local/include/d/dex app.d -L-ldex -of=myapp Option C: Pre-Packaged Minimal Release Archives If you prefer not to clone the full repository or don't have git installed in your build container, you can download minimal standalone release archives (~38 KiB) from the GitHub Releases page. These packages contain only the core library files (source/dex/*.d), LICENSE, dub.json, and Makefile: Terminal # Download and unpack minimal library source package $ curl -fsSL https://github.com/ernlel/dex/releases/download/v0.5.0/dex-0.5.0.tar.gz | tar -xz # Compile your app against the unpacked sources $ dmd -i -Idex-0.5.0/source app.d -of=myapp Zero External Dependencies dex does not require libevent, libuv, OpenSSL, or external C shared libraries. It builds directly against the standard Phobos library with instant compile times.

records.title: Hello World
records.text: Create the most fundamental dex application: an HTTP server responding to requests on port 3000. In your project directory, open source/app.d and write the following code: source/app.d import dex; import std.stdio : writeln; void main() { auto app = new App; app.get("/", (req, res) { res.send("Hello, World!"); }); app.listen(3000, () { writeln("Example app listening on http://localhost:3000"); }); } How It Works import dex; brings in the App class, request/response models, and built-in middleware. auto app = new App; creates a new application instance. App is also a Router, so you can register routes and middleware directly on it. app.get("/", (req, res) { ... }) registers a route handler for HTTP GET requests to the root path (/). The handler receives a Request object (req) and a Response object (res). res.send("Hello, World!") ends the response, sets Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8 (by default for strings), computes Content-Length, and sends the response. app.listen(3000, callback) binds to 0.0.0.0:3000, starts accepting HTTP/1.1 connections, and invokes the callback once the socket is successfully listening. Running the App Run the application using DUB: Terminal $ dub run Point your browser to http://localhost:3000/ or test it in terminal with curl: Terminal $ curl -i http://localhost:3000/ HTTP/1.1 200 OK Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8 Date: Fri, 06 Nov 2026 15:30:00 GMT Server: dex Content-Length: 13 Connection: keep-alive Hello, World!

records.title: Basic Routing
records.text: Routing refers to how an application’s endpoints respond to client requests. You define routing using methods of the dex App instance. Route Structure Route definitions follow this straightforward structure: D app.METHOD(PATH, HANDLER); Where: app is an instance of dex.App. METHOD is an HTTP request method, in lowercase (e.g., get, post, put, delete). PATH is a path string on the server. HANDLER is a callback executed when the route matches: (req, res) { ... }. Basic Examples source/app.d // Respond to GET request on the root URL (/) app.get("/", (req, res) { res.send("GET request to homepage"); }); // Respond to POST request on the root URL (/) app.post("/", (req, res) { res.send("POST request to homepage"); }); // Respond to a PUT request to the /user route app.put("/user", (req, res) { res.send("Got a PUT request at /user"); }); // Respond to a DELETE request to the /user route app.delete("/user", (req, res) { res.send("Got a DELETE request at /user"); }); Route Parameters Route parameters are named URL segments used to capture values at specified positions in the URL. Captured values populate the req.params associative array: Parameters app.get("/users/:userId/books/:bookId", (req, res) { const userId = req.params["userId"]; const bookId = req.params["bookId"]; res.send("User: " ~ userId ~ ", Book: " ~ bookId); }); Query Parameters Read query parameters from the request URL using req.queryParam() or req.queryParams(): D // GET /search?q=dlang&tag=web&tag=fast app.get("/search", (req, res) { const query = req.queryParam("q"); // "dlang" const tags = req.queryParams("tag"); // ["web", "fast"] res.json(["query": query]); }); Response Methods The Response object (res) provides methods to send data back to the client and conclude the request-response cycle: res.send(text) — Sends a string body, defaults to text/html; charset=utf-8. res.json(value) — Serializes any D struct, class, array, or associative array to JSON and sets application/json. res.sendStatus(statusCode) — Sets the status code and sends its reason phrase (e.g., res.sendStatus(404)). res.redirect([status], url) — Issues an HTTP redirect (default 302 Found). res.sendFile(filePath) — Streams a file from disk in 64 KiB chunks with range support.

records.title: Serving Static Files
records.text: Serve images, CSS stylesheets, client-side JavaScript, and media assets using the built-in serveStatic middleware. Basic Usage Pass the path to your static directory to serveStatic(): source/app.d app.use(serveStatic("public")); Now you can load files residing inside the public directory from the root URL: D http://localhost:3000/images/kitten.jpg http://localhost:3000/css/style.css http://localhost:3000/js/app.js http://localhost:3000/hello.html Virtual Path Prefix To create a virtual path prefix (where the prefix does not actually exist in the file system), mount serveStatic under a path: D app.use("/static", serveStatic("public")); Files can now be accessed via the /static path prefix: Text http://localhost:3000/static/images/kitten.jpg http://localhost:3000/static/css/style.css Static Configuration Options Customize static file serving behavior using StaticOptions: D StaticOptions options; options.index = "index.html"; // Default file for directory requests options.cacheControl = "public, max-age=86400"; // Custom Cache-Control header options.dotFiles = false; // Ignore hidden files (.env, .git) app.use(serveStatic("./public", options)); Sending Individual Files from Disk Use res.sendFile(filePath) to send a specific file from disk inside any route handler. Files are streamed in 64 KiB chunks with zero memory accumulation and full support for HTTP Range requests (206 Partial Content): Streaming File app.get("/download/report.pdf", (req, res) { res.sendFile("./data/annual_report.pdf"); }); Audio & Video Seeking Support Because sendFile and serveStatic implement Accept-Ranges: bytes, HTML5 <audio> and <video> players can seek seamlessly forward and backward without downloading the entire media file.

records.title: Frequently Asked Questions
records.text: Quick answers and best practices for common tasks in dex. How do I handle 404 responses? In dex, a 404 response is not the result of an error; it simply indicates that none of your registered route handlers responded to the request. You can define a catch-all handler as the very last middleware: D // Defined at the bottom after all other routes app.use((req, res) { res.status(404).type("text").send("Sorry, can’t find that!"); }); How do I set up custom error handling? Define an error-handling middleware function that takes four parameters: (Throwable error, Request req, Response res, Next next): D app.use((Throwable error, Request req, Response res, Next next) { if (auto httpError = cast(HttpError) error) { res.status(httpError.status).json(["error": httpError.msg]); } else { res.status(500).json(["error": "Internal Server Error"]); } }); How do I read JSON POST bodies? Request bodies with application/json are parsed lazily on first access into req.body. You can extract typed fields directly using req.bodyValue!T("field"): D app.post("/users", (req, res) { const name = req.bodyValue!string("name"); const age = req.bodyValue!int("age"); res.status(201).json(["created": name]); }); How do I enable CORS? Use the built-in cors() middleware: D // Allow all origins app.use(cors()); // Or configure specific origins and credentials CorsOptions corsOptions; corsOptions.origin = "https://myfrontend.com"; corsOptions.credentials = true; app.use(cors(corsOptions)); How do I add security headers (Helmet-style)? Use the built-in securityHeaders() middleware to set X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN, Referrer-Policy, and more: D app.use(securityHeaders()); How do I bind JSON or query parameters into typed D structs? Use req.bind!T() for JSON/form bodies and req.bindQuery!T() for query strings. Both support nested structs, Nullable!T, default values, enums, and @optional, raising descriptive 422/400 HttpError responses when required fields are missing or invalid. How do I run dex behind Nginx or Caddy? Configure app.trustProxy (e.g. app.trustProxy = 1; or app.trustProxy = ["loopback", "10.0.0.0/8"];) so req.ip, req.protocol, req.secure, req.hostname, and rateLimit() use X-Forwarded-* headers safely. How do I use sessions, compression, rate limiting, and per-route body limits? All four ship built-in in dex: app.use(compression()), app.use(rateLimit()), app.use(session(SessionOptions(secret: "..."))), and app.post("/upload", bodyLimit(50 * 1024 * 1024), handler). See the Middleware Guide and Template Engine Guide for details. How does graceful shutdown work? app.listen() automatically catches POSIX SIGINT and SIGTERM (when app.handleSignals = true), stops accepting new connections, closes idle keep-alive sockets, sends Connection: close on in-flight responses, and drains up to app.shutdownTimeout (5 seconds by default).

records.title: Routing in Depth
records.text: Master route matching, wildcards, route chaining, and modular sub-routers with dex. HTTP Verb Methods dex supports all standard HTTP verbs via helper methods on App and Router: get, post, put, patch, delete, head, options, trace, connect, and all. D // Matches any HTTP method on /secret app.all("/secret", (req, res, next) { res.set("x-auth", "checked"); next(); }); Wildcard Route Patterns Use * as the final segment to capture arbitrary path tails. The captured string is accessible via req.params["0"] or req.params["*"]: D app.get("/files/*", (req, res) { const subpath = req.params["0"]; // e.g. "docs/readme.txt" res.send("Requested: " ~ subpath); }); Modular Sub-Routers Use dex.Router to create modular, mountable route handlers. A Router instance is a complete middleware and routing system: source/routes/users.d import dex; Router userRouter() { auto router = new Router; router.get("/", (req, res) { res.json(["users": ["User 1", "User 2"]]); }); router.get("/:id", (req, res) { res.json(["id": req.params["id"]]); }); return router; } Mount the router on a path in your main application: source/app.d app.use("/api/users", userRouter()); Inside the mounted router: req.baseUrl reflects "/api/users". req.path reflects the subpath (e.g. "/" or "/42"). req.originalUrl preserves the full raw URL ("/api/users/42").

records.title: Writing & Using Middleware
records.text: Middleware functions have access to the request object, response object, and the next middleware function in the application’s request-response cycle. Anatomy of a Middleware Function A middleware function is a delegate taking three parameters: Text (Request req, Response res, Next next) { // Do work... next(); // Pass execution to the next handler } Middleware functions can perform the following tasks: Execute any code. Make changes to the request and the response objects. End the request-response cycle by sending data (e.g. res.status(403).send("Forbidden")). Call the next middleware function in the stack using next(). Custom Timing Middleware Example source/app.d app.use((req, res, next) { const start = MonoTime.currTime; res.onFinish((finishedRes) { const ms = (MonoTime.currTime - start).total!"msecs"; writefln("[%s] %s took %d ms", req.method, req.url, ms); }); next(); }); Built-in Middleware dex includes essential, production-ready middleware right out of the box: 1. Logger (logger()) Logs incoming requests, status codes, and latency to stderr (or a custom log sink delegate): D app.use(logger()); 2. Static Files (serveStatic()) Streams static assets from disk in 64 KiB chunks with range support: D app.use(serveStatic("./public")); 3. CORS (cors()) Handles Cross-Origin Resource Sharing headers and preflight OPTIONS requests: D // Allow any origin app.use(cors()); // Or with custom configuration CorsOptions options; options.origin = "https://frontend.com"; options.credentials = true; options.methods = "GET, POST, PUT, DELETE"; app.use(cors(options)); 4. Security Headers (securityHeaders()) Sets standard defensive headers (equivalent to Express Helmet): D app.use(securityHeaders()); 5. Compression (compression()) Compresses response bodies using Gzip or Deflate based on client Accept-Encoding headers and content type (HTML, JSON, JS, CSS, SVG, text). Configure via CompressionOptions (threshold, level, filter): D import dex; // Default compression (threshold 1024 bytes) app.use(compression()); // Custom threshold or compression level (1-9) CompressionOptions options; options.threshold = 512; // Compress payloads >= 512 bytes options.level = 6; app.use(compression(options)); 6. Rate Limiting (rateLimit()) Restricts incoming request volume per client key within a configured time window to protect APIs against abuse and DDoS. Configure via RateLimitOptions (window, max, statusCode, message, standardHeaders, legacyHeaders, keyGenerator, handler, skip): D import dex; import core.time : dur; // Default rate limiter (60 requests per 1 minute per IP) app.use(rateLimit()); // Custom rate limit rules on API routes RateLimitOptions options; options.max = 100; options.window = 15.dur!"minutes"; options.message = "API rate limit exceeded. Please wait before retrying."; app.use("/api", rateLimit(options)); 7. Per-Route Body Size Limits (bodyLimit()) Overrides app.maxBodySize for specific routes or sub-routers, allowing tight caps on JSON endpoints while permitting larger uploads on dedicated routes: D import dex; // Tight global default (64 KiB) app.maxBodySize = 64 * 1024; // Allow up to 50 MiB on a specific upload route app.post("/upload", bodyLimit(50 * 1024 * 1024), (req, res) { res.send("Uploaded " ~ req.rawBody.length.to!string ~ " bytes"); }); 8. Sessions & Signed Cookies (session()) Manages server-side sessions backed by HMAC-SHA256 signed cookies and a pluggable SessionStore (defaulting to thread-safe MemorySessionStore). Configure via SessionOptions (secret, secrets, cookieName, ttl, cookie, store, saveUninitialized, rolling, resave): D import dex; import core.time : dur; app.cookieSecrets = ["primary-secret", "previous-secret"]; app.use(session(SessionOptions(ttl: 24.dur!"hours"))); app.post("/login", (req, res) { req.session.regenerate(); req.session["user"] = "alice"; res.send("logged in"); });

records.text: Handles Cross-Origin Resource Sharing headers and preflight OPTIONS requests: D // Allow any origin app.use(cors()); // Or with custom configuration CorsOptions options; options.origin = "https://frontend.com"; options.credentials = true; options.methods = "GET, POST, PUT, DELETE"; app.use(cors(options));

records.title: 4. Security Headers (securityHeaders())
records.text: Sets standard defensive headers (equivalent to Express Helmet): D app.use(securityHeaders());

records.title: 5. Compression (compression())
records.text: Compresses response bodies using Gzip or Deflate based on client Accept-Encoding headers and content type (HTML, JSON, JS, CSS, SVG, text). Configure via CompressionOptions (threshold, level, filter): D import dex; // Default compression (threshold 1024 bytes) app.use(compression()); // Custom threshold or compression level (1-9) CompressionOptions options; options.threshold = 512; // Compress payloads >= 512 bytes options.level = 6; app.use(compression(options));

records.title: 6. Rate Limiting (rateLimit())
records.text: Restricts incoming request volume per client key within a configured time window to protect APIs against abuse and DDoS. Configure via RateLimitOptions (window, max, statusCode, message, standardHeaders, legacyHeaders, keyGenerator, handler, skip): D import dex; import core.time : dur; // Default rate limiter (60 requests per 1 minute per IP) app.use(rateLimit()); // Custom rate limit rules on API routes RateLimitOptions options; options.max = 100; options.window = 15.dur!"minutes"; options.message = "API rate limit exceeded. Please wait before retrying."; app.use("/api", rateLimit(options));

records.title: 7. Per-Route Body Size Limits (bodyLimit())
records.text: Overrides app.maxBodySize for specific routes or sub-routers, allowing tight caps on JSON endpoints while permitting larger uploads on dedicated routes: D import dex; // Tight global default (64 KiB) app.maxBodySize = 64 * 1024; // Allow up to 50 MiB on a specific upload route app.post("/upload", bodyLimit(50 * 1024 * 1024), (req, res) { res.send("Uploaded " ~ req.rawBody.length.to!string ~ " bytes"); });

records.title: 8. Sessions & Signed Cookies (session())
records.text: Manages server-side sessions backed by HMAC-SHA256 signed cookies and a pluggable SessionStore (defaulting to thread-safe MemorySessionStore). Configure via SessionOptions (secret, secrets, cookieName, ttl, cookie, store, saveUninitialized, rolling, resave): D import dex; import core.time : dur; app.cookieSecrets = ["primary-secret", "previous-secret"]; app.use(session(SessionOptions(ttl: 24.dur!"hours"))); app.post("/login", (req, res) { req.session.regenerate(); req.session["user"] = "alice"; res.send("logged in"); });

records.title: Error Handling
records.text: Learn how dex catches synchronous and asynchronous exceptions and routes them through your error middleware pipeline. Throwing HttpError When an error occurs in your business logic that corresponds to a specific HTTP status code (such as 400 Bad Request or 404 Not Found), throw HttpError: Throwing HttpError app.get("/users/:id", (req, res) { const user = findUser(req.params["id"]); if (user is null) throw new HttpError(404, "User not found"); res.json(user); }); Writing Error-Handling Middleware Error-handling middleware functions are defined with four arguments: (Throwable error, Request req, Response res, Next next). They only execute when an exception is thrown or when next(error) is called: Error Middleware app.use((Throwable error, Request req, Response res, Next next) { if (auto httpError = cast(HttpError) error) { res.status(httpError.status).json([ "status": httpError.status, "error": httpError.msg ]); } else { res.status(500).json([ "status": 500, "error": "Internal Server Error" ]); } }); Default Server Error Handler If an error is thrown and no error-handling middleware ends the response: dex catches the error, sets status 500 Internal Server Error (or the HttpError.status code), and returns a plain text error message. When app.logErrors = true (default), 5xx server errors are written to stderr with stack traces. When app.showStackTraces = true, the full exception string is sent to the HTTP client (useful during development).

records.title: App
records.text: The top-level application class inheriting from Router and managing the HTTP/1.1 lifecycle. Properties & Configuration idleTimeout: Duration — Keep-alive socket idle timeout (default: 60.seconds). shutdownTimeout: Duration — Maximum time close() waits for in-flight requests to drain (default: 5.seconds). handleSignals: bool — Install POSIX SIGINT/SIGTERM graceful shutdown hooks during listen() and wait() (default: true). maxBodySize: size_t — Maximum accepted request body in bytes (default: 10 MiB). maxHeaderSize: size_t — Maximum accepted header bytes (default: 64 KiB). maxConnections: size_t — Max concurrent TCP connections; 0 means unlimited (default: 1024). trustProxy: TrustProxy — Reverse-proxy trust policy (bool, hop count, or IP/CIDR list) for X-Forwarded-* headers (default: disabled). etag: bool — Automatically generate ETag headers and return 304 Not Modified on matching conditional requests (default: true). handleMethodNotAllowed: bool — Respond with 405 Method Not Allowed and an Allow header when a path matches other HTTP methods (default: false). cookieSecret: string / cookieSecrets: string[] — HMAC-SHA256 secret(s) for signed cookies (supports key rotation). showStackTraces: bool — Send exception stack traces to clients on 500 errors (default: false). logErrors: bool — Write unhandled 5xx errors to stderr (default: true). caseSensitive: bool — Enable case-sensitive route matching (default: false). viewsDir: string — Directory where templates reside (default: "./views"). defaultViewEngine: string — Default view extension (default: "html"). cacheViews: bool — Enable in-memory compiled template caching (default: false). isListening: bool — Whether the server is currently accepting connections. port: ushort — The bound TCP port (especially useful with ephemeral port listen(0)). Methods app.listen(port, host = "0.0.0.0", onReady = null) Binds the HTTP server to the given port and blocks until the server closes. If port == 0, the OS assigns an ephemeral free port. app.start(port, host = "0.0.0.0", onReady = null) Starts accepting connections on a background accept thread without blocking the calling thread. Read the bound port from app.port. app.close([timeout]) Stops accepting incoming connections, closes idle keep-alive sockets immediately, signals in-flight responses with Connection: close, and waits up to timeout (defaults to shutdownTimeout) for active requests to complete before forcing remaining connections closed. app.use([prefix], handler | middleware | router) Registers middleware or mounts a sub-router, optionally under a URL prefix. app.setViews(directory) Sets the filesystem directory where view templates are located. Defaults to "./views". Returns this. app.viewEngine(extension) Sets the default view file extension (e.g. "html") used when res.render() is called without a file extension. Returns this. app.engine(extension, renderer) Registers a custom template engine delegate for the specified file extension with signature string delegate(string templatePath, JSONValue locals). Returns this. app.renderView(viewName, locals) Compiles and renders a view template file by name with the given JSON locals. Used internally by res.render().

records.text: Represents the incoming HTTP request, including headers, query parameters, route parameters, cookies, and body. Properties app: App — The application instance handling this request. method: string — Uppercase HTTP method (e.g. "GET", "POST"). httpVersion: string — HTTP protocol version (e.g. "HTTP/1.1"). url: string — Request path plus query string (e.g. "/search?q=dlang"). path: string — Decoded URL path (e.g. "/files/my doc.pdf"). rawPath: string — Raw percent-encoded URL path. originalUrl: string — Unmodified request target before any router prefix trimming. baseUrl: string — URL path prefix where the current router was mounted. queryString: string — Raw query string without leading ?. params: string[string] — Associative array of named route parameters (e.g. req.params["id"]). query: string[string] — Parsed query parameters (last value wins). queryAll: string[][string] — All query parameter values in order. headers: string[][string] — Request headers keyed by lowercased name. cookies: string[string] — Parsed request cookies. signedCookies: string[string] — HMAC-verified signed cookies (populated when app.cookieSecret is set). session: Session — Active server-side session attached by session() middleware, or null. body: JSONValue — Parsed request body (lazily evaluated on first access). rawBody: string — Raw unparsed request body as a string (lazily loaded from socket). maxBodySize: size_t — Effective maximum body size in bytes for this request (from app.maxBodySize or bodyLimit()). ip: string — Client IP address string (resolved through app.trustProxy when enabled). ips: string[] — Proxy IP chain from client to nearest proxy when app.trustProxy is enabled. protocol: string — "http" or "https". secure: bool — True if the request arrived over TLS or trusted X-Forwarded-Proto: https. xhr: bool — True if X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest was present. fresh: bool / stale: bool — Whether the client's conditional request (If-None-Match / If-Modified-Since) matches the response. Methods req.get(name) / req.header(name) Returns the value of the specified HTTP header (case-insensitive). If multiple values are present, they are joined with commas. req.getValues(name) Returns all raw values for the header as a string[] array. req.param(name) Returns a matched route parameter, or null if missing. req.queryParam(name) Returns the query parameter value, or null. req.queryParams(name) Returns all query parameter values matching name as a string[]. req.cookie(name) Returns the parsed cookie value, or null. req.signedCookie(name, [secret]) Returns the HMAC-SHA256 verified signed cookie value, or null if missing or tampered. req.bodyValue!T(name) Extracts a typed field from a JSON object or URL-encoded body. Throws HttpError(400) if the field is missing or has the wrong type. req.bind!T([errorStatus = 422]) / req.bindQuery!T([errorStatus = 400]) Deserializes and validates JSON/form bodies (bind!T) or query parameters (bindQuery!T) into nested D structs with support for Nullable!T, default field values, enums, arrays, and @optional. records.title: Response (res)
records.text:
The Response object represents the HTTP response that an HTTP server sends when it receives an HTTP request. In handlers, the response object is customarily referred to as res (or response). Most methods on Response return this to allow method chaining. Properties res.app The App instance handling this response. res.statusCode The integer HTTP status code that will be sent to the client (e.g. 200, 404, 500). Defaults to 200. res.headersSent / res.finished Boolean property that indicates if the response has been sent/finished. Once true, subsequent header or body writes are ignored. Methods res.status(code) Sets the HTTP status code. Returns this for chaining. D res.status(404).send("Page Not Found"); res.status(201).json(createdRecord); res.set(name, value) / res.header(name, value) Sets an HTTP header field to the specified value. Header names are case-insensitive. Values are checked to prevent CRLF injection. D res.set("X-Powered-By", "dex") .set("Cache-Control", "no-cache"); res.append(name, value) Appends a value to an existing header. If the header does not yet exist, it creates it. For regular headers, values are separated by a comma and space. For Set-Cookie, multiple headers are emitted. D res.append("Warning", "199 Miscellaneous warning"); res.get(name) Returns the value of the HTTP response header specified by name (case-insensitive), or null if not set. res.has(name) Returns true if the specified response header has been set, false otherwise. res.type(contentType) / res.contentType(contentType) Sets the Content-Type HTTP header to the MIME type looked up by extension (e.g. "json", "html", "png", "pdf") or a full MIME type string. D res.type("json"); // Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8 res.type("html"); // Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8 res.type("png"); // Content-Type: image/png res.send(body) Sends the HTTP response with a text/HTML body and ends the response. If no Content-Type has been set, it defaults to text/html; charset=utf-8. D res.send("Hello World"); res.type("text/plain").send("Raw plaintext content"); res.sendBytes(bytes) Sends raw binary data (const(ubyte)[]) and ends the response. Defaults to application/octet-stream if no Content-Type has been set. res.json(value) / res.sendJson(value) Serializes any D value (struct, class, array, associative array, primitive, or JSONValue) to a JSON string, sets Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8, and ends the response. D struct User { string name; int id; } res.json(User("Alice", 42)); res.render(viewName, [locals]) Renders a view template using the application's view engine, sets Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8, and ends the response. locals can be any D struct, class, associative array, or JSONValue. See the Template Engine Guide for details. D struct PageData { string title; string user; } res.render("index", PageData("Home", "Example User")); // Without locals: res.render("about"); res.sendFile(filePath) Streams a file from the filesystem to the client in 64 KiB chunks. Automatically detects Content-Type, sets Last-Modified and weak ETag, handles 304 Not Modified conditional requests, announces Accept-Ranges: bytes, and handles Range requests (206 Partial Content / 416 Range Not Satisfiable). D res.sendFile("./public/downloads/manual.pdf"); res.download(filePath, [filename]) Sends filePath as an attachment download with a sanitized Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="..." header (and RFC 5987 filename* for non-ASCII names). D res.download("./reports/q4.pdf", "quarterly-report.pdf"); res.etag(tag) Sets the ETag response header explicitly. Dynamic 200 responses also receive an automatic SHA-256 ETag when app.etag is enabled. res.format(handlers) Performs content negotiation on the request's Accept header, sets the matched Content-Type, and invokes the matching handler (or "default", or throws HttpError(406)). D res.format([ "html": (Request req, Response res) { res.send("

records.title: res.statusCode
records.text: The integer HTTP status code that will be sent to the client (e.g. 200, 404, 500). Defaults to 200.

records.title: res.headersSent / res.finished
records.text: Boolean property that indicates if the response has been sent/finished. Once true, subsequent header or body writes are ignored.

records.title: res.status(code)

records.title: res.set(name, value) / res.header(name, value)
records.text: Sets an HTTP header field to the specified value. Header names are case-insensitive. Values are checked to prevent CRLF injection. D res.set("X-Powered-By", "dex") .set("Cache-Control", "no-cache");

records.title: res.append(name, value)
records.text: Appends a value to an existing header. If the header does not yet exist, it creates it. For regular headers, values are separated by a comma and space. For Set-Cookie, multiple headers are emitted. D res.append("Warning", "199 Miscellaneous warning");

records.title: res.get(name)
records.text: Returns the value of the HTTP response header specified by name (case-insensitive), or null if not set.

records.title: res.has(name)
records.text: Returns true if the specified response header has been set, false otherwise.

records.title: res.type(contentType) / res.contentType(contentType)
records.text: Sets the Content-Type HTTP header to the MIME type looked up by extension (e.g. "json", "html", "png", "pdf") or a full MIME type string. D res.type("json"); // Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8 res.type("html"); // Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8 res.type("png"); // Content-Type: image/png

records.title: res.send(body)
records.text: Sends the HTTP response with a text/HTML body and ends the response. If no Content-Type has been set, it defaults to text/html; charset=utf-8. D res.send("Hello World"); res.type("text/plain").send("Raw plaintext content");

records.title: res.sendBytes(bytes)
records.text: Sends raw binary data (const(ubyte)[]) and ends the response. Defaults to application/octet-stream if no Content-Type has been set.

records.title: res.json(value) / res.sendJson(value)
records.text: Serializes any D value (struct, class, array, associative array, primitive, or JSONValue) to a JSON string, sets Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8, and ends the response. D struct User { string name; int id; } res.json(User("Alice", 42));

records.title: res.render(viewName, [locals])
records.text: Renders a view template using the application's view engine, sets Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8, and ends the response. locals can be any D struct, class, associative array, or JSONValue. See the Template Engine Guide for details. D struct PageData { string title; string user; } res.render("index", PageData("Home", "Example User")); // Without locals: res.render("about");

records.title: res.sendFile(filePath)
records.text: Streams a file from the filesystem to the client in 64 KiB chunks. Automatically detects Content-Type, sets Last-Modified and weak ETag, handles 304 Not Modified conditional requests, announces Accept-Ranges: bytes, and handles Range requests (206 Partial Content / 416 Range Not Satisfiable). records.title: res.etag(tag)

Performs content negotiation on the request's Accept header, sets the matched Content-Type, and invokes the matching handler (or "default", or throws HttpError(406)). D res.format([ "html": (Request req, Response res) { res.send("

records.title: res.closeConnection()
records.text: Instructs the server to add Connection: close and shut down the underlying TCP connection immediately after sending this response, even on HTTP/1.1 keep-alive connections.

records.title: Router
records.text: A Router instance is a complete middleware and routing system; for this reason, it is often referred to as a "mini-app". Every dex application (App) inherits from Router. You can also instantiate isolated Router instances and mount them on paths using app.use("/prefix", router). Instantiation D import dex; auto router = new Router(); Properties router.caseSensitive Enables case-sensitive route matching. Defaults to false (meaning /Users matches /users). D router.caseSensitive = true; Methods router.use([path], [middleware...]) Mounts middleware or a sub-router on this router. If path is specified, the middleware only runs for paths matching that prefix. D // Runs on every request passing through this router router.use((req, res, next) { // perform check or authentication next(); }); // Runs only under /api router.use("/api", (req, res, next) { next(); }); router.use(ErrorHandler) Registers an error-handling middleware delegate with signature void delegate(Throwable error, Request req, Response res, Next next). D router.use((err, req, res, next) { res.status(500).send("Router Error: " ~ err.msg); }); router.use([path], Router) Mounts a sub-router. When requests match path, req.baseUrl is updated to include the prefix and req.path is adjusted to the remainder of the path. D auto api = new Router(); auto v1 = new Router(); v1.get("/users", (req, res) => res.json(["Alice", "Bob"])); api.use("/v1", v1); app.use("/api", api); // Matches GET /api/v1/users router.METHOD(path, [middleware...], handler) Registers one or more middlewares followed by a route handler for specific HTTP methods (variadic handler chains are supported). Supported methods include: router.get(path, ...) (also responds to HEAD requests) router.post(path, ...) router.put(path, ...) router.delete(path, ...) (or delete_) router.patch(path, ...) router.head(path, ...) router.options(path, ...) router.connect(path, ...) router.trace(path, ...) router.param(name, callback) Registers a parameter pre-handler void delegate(Request req, Response res, Next next, string value) invoked once per request whenever route parameter name is matched. D router.param("id", (req, res, next, id) { // validate or preload entity by id next(); }); router.route(path) Returns a fluent RouteChain builder for registering multiple HTTP methods on the same path (use .del(...) or .delete_(...) for DELETE): D router.route("/items/:id") .get((req, res) { res.send("get " ~ req.param("id")); }) .put((req, res) { res.send("put " ~ req.param("id")); }) .del((req, res) { res.send("del " ~ req.param("id")); }); D router.get("/items", (req, res) { res.json(items); }); router.post("/items", (req, res) { // create item res.status(201).json(created); }); router.all(path, handler | middleware) Matches any HTTP method for the given path. D router.all("/secret", (req, res, next) { // runs for GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, etc. next(); }); router.route(method, path, handler | middleware) Registers a route handler for an arbitrary custom or extended HTTP verb (e.g. SEARCH, PURGE, LINK). D router.route("PURGE", "/cache", (req, res) { clearCache(); res.send("Cache purged"); }); Modular Architecture Example Separate your application into domain-driven modules: D // routes/users.d module routes.users; import dex; Router usersRouter() { auto r = new Router(); r.get("/", (req, res) => res.json(allUsers())); r.get("/:id", (req, res) { auto user = findUser(req.param("id")); if (!user.found) throw new HttpError(404, "User not found"); res.json(user); }); return r; } // app.d import dex; import routes.users; void main() { auto app = dex.app(); app.use("/users", usersRouter()); app.listen(3000); }
